# [Tailwind CSS Fade In Animation - React Vite App](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xG4lp3KGqoI)

**Visibility**: Public
**Uploaded by**: [Mitter - Your Tech Mate](https://www.youtube.com/@mitter-yourtechmate4376)
**Uploaded at**: 2025-07-11
**Published at**: 
**Length**: 11:19
**Views**: 1686
**Likes**: 18
**Category**: Howto & Style

## Description

```
Learn how to build a smooth fade-in animation in React using Tailwind CSS — this animation works both on page load and on scroll!

Got questions? Drop them in the comments below — I respond to everyone.

Related Videos you might enjoy:
https://youtu.be/qkbijl5EoHc
https://youtu.be/6-0j8P-4XvY
https://youtu.be/ku99cfuK5wg
https://youtu.be/kKb_HoZb3NI

Need help with your project?
https://www.fiverr.com/s/BReyq8y
https://shankeyraheja.com/
```

# Animations with Tailwind CSS

## Transition, the hidden star of Headless UI.

[![Markus Tripp](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fill:32:32/1*hT2puZkz0nERX1-7VTDDJw.jpeg)](https://markustripp.medium.com/?source=post_page---byline--c47534e57a18---------------------------------------)

[Markus Tripp](https://markustripp.medium.com/?source=post_page---byline--c47534e57a18---------------------------------------)

Follow

2

[Listen](https://medium.com/m/signin?actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fmedium.com%2Fplans%3Fdimension%3Dpost_audio_button%26postId%3Dc47534e57a18&operation=register&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmarkustripp.medium.com%2Fanimations-with-tailwind-css-c47534e57a18&source=---header_actions--c47534e57a18---------------------post_audio_button------------------)

Share

The best mobile apps, like Airbnb and Spotify, are fun to use. But what makes them so great? Yes, they have an outstanding UI and UX. But what separates them are these little animations on page transitions and for other user interactions.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Airbnb animations on mobile (iPhone)](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*8EluBAhelY8Y2ttTlwvIaw.gif)

Airbnb animations on mobile (iPhone)

I create web apps, and most of the time, I use [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling.

_How can I add those little animations to my web projects with Tailwind CSS?_

Of course, I can use a library like [Framer Motion](https://www.framer.com/motion/). It’s fantastic, but in this article, I will show you how you can use the amazing [Headless UI Transition component](https://headlessui.com/react/transition) in combination with [Tailwind CSS native animation properties](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/transition-property) to achieve great results.

I’m implementing two common use cases:

### Animated form input elements in a slide-over panel

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Tailwind CSS animation: Animated form input elements that slide over](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*Q9FUL1dfitKV54ApVDRYaw.gif)

### Elements that fade in when they enter the viewport

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Tailwind CSS animation: Elements that fade in when they enter the viewport](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*InfxqD6x5MrrT_vXoAV_qw.gif)

Elements that fade in when they enter the viewport

Find the source code of all steps from the beginning to the final working examples on my public GitHub repository:

[markustripp/tailwind-animation](https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation).

## Animated Input Elements

I assume you are familiar with setting up a [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) project with [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/installation), [Tailwind Forms](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss-forms), and [Headless UI](https://headlessui.com/). If not, tons of tutorials show you how to do that.

### **Step 1: Create Page Structure**

First, create a page with two simple components: a `Button` component and an `Input` component. Clicking the button toggles the input field.

> I’ll name the example pages slide1.js, slide2.js, slide3.js, … each number for each step during the development.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Clicking a button toggles the input field](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*AXO2oXTF2SsSkGuLnAroBw.gif)

Example Step 1: Create Page Structure

[https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide1.js](https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide1.js)

### **Step 2: Add Headless UI Transition**

Now, when clicking the button, I want to trigger the animation and fade in the input field. You control this by linking the `Transition` show attribute with the show state variable.

For the fade-in animation, you set the following attributes:

- Opacity from zero to 100%
- Translate-y from 6 to zero to move the element up during fading in

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Clicking the button triggers the input field to fade-in.](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*HCekZSSMjV5K56xN7rsF5A.gif)

Example Step 2: Add Headless UI Transition

[https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide2.js](https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide2.js)

### **Step 3: Introducing Transition.Root and Transition.Child**

On button click, I want to animate multiple form elements individually. Therefore I must convert the `Transition` component to `Transition.Child` components and wrap it with a `Transition.Root` component.

The `Transition.Root`component is linked to the show state variable and controls when all child components get triggered.

[https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide3.js](https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide3.js)

### **Step 4: Create FadeIn Component**

For re-usability and readability, I convert the `Transition.Child` animation into a `FadeIn` component. This enables me to apply the `FadeIn` component to multiple fields easily.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Clicking the button triggers the input fields to fade-in individually.](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*dHfcSNYjhG921zrB6D-Q_w.gif)

Example Step 4: Create FadeIn Component

[https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide4.js](https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide4.js)

Please note that each input field starts the animation with a different delay:

- First name: `delay-[0ms]`
- Last name: `delay-[300ms]`
- Email: `delay-[500ms]`

> **Note:** For the Tailwind CSS compiler to work properly, the attributes must be available in clear text. E.g., it is not possible to use variables for the milliseconds like `delay-[${index * 100}ms]`

### **Step 5: Add Background and SlideOver layer**

Next, I want a panel with the form to slide in when the button is clicked. To create this effect, you must create two extra layers:

- **BackgroundLayer**
- **SlideOverLayer** with a panel that fades in the form input fields

Press enter or click to view image in full size![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:1040/1*1umsKLcJ6lfJAhR9OxyJ2w.png)

Press enter or click to view image in full size![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:1499/1*QD9riPNnmXyRKzv6w2RWsA.png)

> To prevent scrolling of the underlying layer, I use a combination of `fixed inset-0`and `absolute` properties.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Slide over panel when button is clicked](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*RCNTVaSKwoqgboQZxdT-lg.gif)

Example Step 5: Add Background and SlideOver layer

[https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide5.js](https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide5.js)

### **Step 6: Animate Form Elements on SlideOverLayer**

As the final step, I add an animation to the BackgroundLayer and SlideOverLayer and fade in the form input fields.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Animate form input fields on slide-over panel](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*Q9FUL1dfitKV54ApVDRYaw.gif)

Example Step 6: Animate Form Elements on SlideOverLayer

[https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide6.js](https://github.com/markustripp/tailwind-animation/blob/main/pages/slide6.js)

> In addition, you should add a [Dialog](https://headlessui.com/react/dialog) component to the slide-over layer as described in the [Tailwind UI component library](https://tailwindui.com/components/application-ui/overlays/slide-overs).

### **Library Ideas**

Steps 1 to 6 helped me create my own component library for my projects.

## Get Markus Tripp’s stories in your inbox

Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer.

Subscribe

Subscribe

Remember me for faster sign in

But `slide7.js`and `slide8.js` include some ideas on how to structure and name a general animation library using this technique. Feel free to add your ideas in the comments below.

> Creating such a library is technically pretty simple. The hard part is naming it properly and adding default animations that are smooth and look awesome on many different use cases.
>
> Please note: slide7.js and slide8.js are just ideas and **NOT** ready libraries and **NOT** tested! Don’t report bugs in the comments.

This example replaces the `Transition.Root` component with an `Animate` component. And a general purpose `SlideOver` is introduced and can be re-used in many projects.

The children of this `Animate.Group` component are faded in using a linear timing.

## Animate on Entering Viewport

Another common use case is to trigger an animation when an element or elements enter the viewport. Either the animation starts immediately or with an offset.

This example fades in a box that includes a header and paragraph when the box enters the viewport. Each element is animated individually.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![Animate a box and individual elements on entering the viewport.](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*InfxqD6x5MrrT_vXoAV_qw.gif)

Final Result: Animate Box and Box Elements on Entering the Viewport

First, I must get notified when an element enters the viewport. All modern browsers implement the [Intersection Observer API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Intersection_Observer_API). But instead of using the native API, I use the [react-intersection-observer](https://react-intersection-observer.vercel.app/) library.

For this use case, I used the `InView` component. It contains a boolean property named `inView`. This property is true when the referenced `ref` element is inside the viewport and false otherwise. Now I link the `inView` property with the `show` property of the `Transition.Root` component.

### **Step 1: Create Page Structure**

I start creating the page without the animation effect. It is just a centered box within a container. For this example, the container has the height of the entire screen.

### **Step 2: Add Animation**

Similar to the slide-over example, I add a `Transition.Root` and multiple `Transition.Child` components.

When the second box enters the viewport, the `inView` variable is set to true, which triggers the animation of the `Transition.Child` elements in the box.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*InfxqD6x5MrrT_vXoAV_qw.gif)

### **Step 3: Library Ideas**

A possible usage of an animation library could look like that:

## Conclusion

You will be surprised by what you can do with just the standard tools from Headless UI and Tailwind CSS. If you have advanced requirements for your animations, you can use a library like Framer Motion. But most of the time, using the standard tools is sufficient.

Press enter or click to view image in full size

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*vQ5wiHYnJTmNLOEdo8pfmA.gif)

Over time, I created a set of animation components that I use across my projects.
